normalization: Compare decoded DNS behavior, execution status, RFC findings, transport type, response matching, and capture completeness.
Ignore run IDs, timestamps, durations, local/remote endpoint addresses, transaction IDs, generated 32-hex nonces, and socket read/write chunking.

Ignore all differences between positive record TTL values, including configured TTL changes; retain zero versus positive. Use Exact evidence when TTL policy matters. Record order within a section and DNS message arrival order are ignored; duplicates and section placement remain significant.

For RRSIG, ignore signature bytes and changing inception/expiry values while retaining their validity at each lookup's recorded timestamp, covered type, algorithm, labels, original TTL, key tag, and signer.
Raw byte-only changes, including opaque malformed payloads, require Exact evidence mode. No changed result is automatically labelled a product fault.

notes: Native UDP/TCP probes; OS caches, private DNS, and VPN interception are not inferred from discovery.
Fresh questions avoid exact-name cache hits; external wildcard synthesis and fixed DNSSEC metadata may still involve caches.

Explicit authoritative endpoint control for the six public additional-data tests only. This differs from normal system-DNS collection; interception is not inferred from the socket destination. Original wire evidence is preserved.
Publication omits local socket endpoint metadata; DNS wire data and remaining evidence are unchanged. Full local captures retained by the operator.

volatility: run_id, timestamps, durations, message IDs, local ports, nonces and nonce-bearing owners/targets
TTL, signature inception/expiration/signature bytes, and record ordering may vary; the external comparator chooses its policy
